summary: Iteration 4: verified Emergent OAuth (/api/auth/session) was fully removed and new direct Google Sign-In endpoint POST /api/auth/google is wired correctly. Added new test suite /app/backend/tests/test_auth_google.py (10 tests) covering: (a) legacy /api/auth/session now returns 404, (b) /api/auth/google returns 422 with no body / wrong type, (c) 401 with 'ID token inválido' on garbage string, (d) 401 on JWT signed with a foreign key (well-formed but not from Google), (e) backend .env exposes non-empty GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com, (f) /api/auth/logout revokes the session_token in the shared user_sessions collection (same behavior would apply to a Google-issued session — same code path). Full backend suite: 52/52 PASSED (was 41 previous + 10 new Google + 1 rewritten legacy). Also refactored one stale test in test_trivia_backend.py::TestAuth::test_invalid_session that still targeted the removed /auth/session endpoint; renamed to test_legacy_session_endpoint_removed and added test_invalid_google_id_token. No regressions in email/password login, forgot/reset password, admin JWT compat, rate limits, questions/answers, prizes, raffles, or notifications. Backend startup log shows google-auth 2.55.1 imported cleanly (no crash on module load — only pre-existing benign passlib/bcrypt WARNING). Happy-path Google login was NOT tested (would need a real google-signed id_token or in-process mocking of google_id_token.verify_oauth2_token; per the request note this is optional).

minor.issue: server.py:517-530 passes audience=None to google_id_token.verify_oauth2_token, then manually validates aud against ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES afterwards (server.py:536-538). This is functionally OK, but Google's library supports passing a list/set of audiences directly; passing None disables the library-side aud check which is acceptable only because the manual check runs immediately after. Consider passing `audience=list(ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES)` (or leaving the current pattern with a code comment) so the intent is explicit.

backend/.env has WEB and ANDROID client IDs but no iOS client id. If iOS build is planned, add GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID; the code (server.py:42-45) already reads it and would include it in ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES.
passlib 1.7.4 still emits 'module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' at startup. Non-blocking (hashing works). Same as iteration 3.
server.py is ~1373 lines. Consider splitting auth into /app/backend/routers/auth.py (informational, not blocking). Same as iteration 3.

action_items: Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: remove the line documenting POST /api/auth/session (it no longer exists) and replace it with POST /api/auth/google (accepts {id_token} from @react-native-google-signin/google-signin, returns {session_token, user}).
OPTIONAL: pass audience=list(ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES) to google_id_token.verify_oauth2_token to make the aud check explicit at the library level (currently done manually just after — still safe).
OPTIONAL: add GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID to backend/.env if an iOS build is planned.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:15-16 imports google.oauth2.id_token + google.auth.transport.requests at module top — correct; no lazy-import needed. Backend restarts cleanly (verified in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log).
server.py:43-45 ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES computed at import-time as the set of non-empty client IDs. Test confirms it contains at least GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID.

server.py:517-587 /auth/google: correctly (1) verifies token signature with google-auth, (2) validates iss (accepts both accounts.google.com and https://accounts.google.com), (3) validates aud against ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES, (4) enforces email_verified, (5) creates OR updates user (idempotent), (6) auto-grants is_admin when email==ADMIN_EMAIL, (7) inserts a session in the SAME user_sessions collection used by local auth so /auth/logout works uniformly.

server.py:706-711 /auth/logout only splits authorization if it exists — but earlier in get_current_user (server.py:262-263) the presence and 'bearer ' prefix are already validated, so authorization.split() here is safe. Good.
MongoDB _id correctly excluded via projections in all Google/session handlers.
SECURITY: ALLOWED_GOOGLE_AUDIENCES is enforced (aud not in set → 401 'Audiencia no permitida'), so a Google-signed token issued for another app's client_id cannot be used to authenticate here.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Google Sign-In direct endpoint (POST /api/auth/google) is live. Happy-path (valid Google id_token → session issued) is NOT covered by automated tests because it requires either (a) a real Google-signed token from an OAuth flow or (b) monkey-patching google_id_token.verify_oauth2_token in-process — not doable through the public HTTP surface. If future testing needs happy-path coverage, add an in-process test that patches google_id_token.verify_oauth2_token to return a fake payload and calls the endpoint via TestClient/httpx directly on the ASGI app (not through the ingress). Legacy /api/auth/session is fully removed. All other flows unchanged. /app/memory/test_credentials.md still documents the removed endpoint — should be updated by main agent.
